title_en: The Great Wall: Myth and Fact
author: Text and translation by Claude (Anthropic)

segs.en: The Great Wall is one of the most famous buildings in China, and one of the most famous ancient structures in the world.
Chinese people often call it the “Ten-Thousand-Li Great Wall”, meaning that it is very, very long.
People say many things about the Great Wall: some of them are true, and some are only legends.
For example, many people think the Great Wall is one long wall that a single emperor built in a short time; others say that you can see it with the naked eye from space.
Are these claims right? Let us take a look together.

zh: 长城是中国最有名的建筑之一，也是世界上最有名的古代建筑之一。中国人常常叫它“万里长城”，意思是它非常非常长。关于长城，人们有很多说法，有的是真的，有的只是传说。比如，很多人以为长城是一道很长的墙、是一个皇帝在很短的时间里修好的；还有人说，从太空中用眼睛就能看到长城。这些说法对不对呢？下面我们一起来看一看。

segs.en: Not One Wall, but Many

zh: 不是一道墙，而是很多道墙

segs.en: In fact, the Great Wall is not one wall but many walls.
They were built over more than two thousand years by different states and dynasties.
As early as the Warring States period, more than two thousand years ago, China was not yet unified, and there were many states in the north and on the Central Plains.
These states often fought one another, and further north lived nomadic peoples who frequently rode south.
To protect themselves, many states built long walls along their borders. These were the earliest Great Walls.

zh: 其实，长城不是一道墙，而是很多道墙。它们是在两千多年里，由不同的国家和朝代修建的。早在两千多年前的战国时期，中国还没有统一，北方和中原有很多国家。这些国家之间常常打仗，北边还有经常南下的游牧民族。为了保护自己，很多国家都在边界上修了长长的墙，这就是最早的长城。

segs.en: In 221 BC, Qin Shi Huang unified China.
tok: Qin Shi Huang, the First Emperor

segs.en: He sent his general Meng Tian with several hundred thousand men to join up the walls that the states of Qin, Zhao and Yan had built in the north, and to build many new sections as well.
In this way the north had, for the first time, a single connected wall, which was used to keep out attacks by the Xiongnu.
Most of the Qin wall was made of earth, and not much of it can still be seen today.

zh: 公元前二百二十一年，秦始皇统一了中国。他让大将蒙恬带着几十万人，把原来秦、赵、燕三个国家在北方修的长城连接起来，又修了很多新的部分。这样，北方第一次有了一道连在一起的长城，用来防止匈奴人的进攻。秦朝的长城大部分是用土修的，今天能看到的已经不多了。

segs.en: In the Han dynasty, the wall grew longer still.
To protect the Silk Road leading to the west, the Han carried the wall all the way into the western deserts.
Near Dunhuang in today's Gansu, you can still see Han walls and beacon towers from two thousand years ago.
tok: Dunhuang, an oasis city in Gansu

segs.en: Many later dynasties built walls too, some a great deal, some only a little.

zh: 汉朝的时候，长城又变得更长了。为了保护通往西方的丝绸之路，汉朝把长城一直修到了西边的沙漠里。在今天甘肃的敦煌附近，人们还能看到两千年前的汉长城和烽火台。后来的很多朝代也修过长城，有的修得多，有的修得少。

segs.en: The Great Wall we see today, especially the tall, massive brick sections near Beijing, was mostly built by the Ming dynasty.
The Ming dynasty lasted from 1368 to 1644, more than two hundred years in all.
Throughout this time, the Ming were building wall almost without a break.
It is often said that the Ming wall “begins at Shanhaiguan in the east and ends at Jiayuguan in the west”, but in fact its eastern end reaches as far as Liaoning.
According to a survey in 2009, the Ming wall is a little over 8,800 kilometres long in total.
If you add together the walls built by every dynasty in history, the total length is more than twenty thousand kilometres.
So “ten thousand li” is no exaggeration at all.
Ten thousand li in the old measure is about five thousand kilometres, and the total length of the walls is more than four times that.

zh: 我们今天看到的长城，特别是北京附近那些用砖修的、又高又大的长城，大部分是明朝修的。明朝从1368年到1644年，一共两百多年。这段时间里，明朝几乎一直在修长城。人们常说，明长城“东起山海关，西到嘉峪关”，其实它的东边一直到了辽宁。根据2009年的测量，明长城一共有八千八百多公里。如果把历史上所有朝代修的长城加在一起，总长度有两万多公里。所以，“万里”一点也不夸张。古代的一万里大约是五千公里，而长城的总长度是它的四倍还多。

segs.en: How the Wall Was Built

zh: 长城是怎么修的

segs.en: When building the wall, people generally used whatever materials they could find locally.
On the northern plains, the most common method was rammed earth: first a frame was made from wooden boards, then earth was poured in and pounded firm with tools, layer by layer.
Earth walls made this way are extremely solid; some have been standing for more than two thousand years.
In the western deserts, where there was little earth, people laid sand, small stones and reeds together in alternating layers.

zh: 修长城的时候，人们一般用的是当地能找到的材料。在北方的平原上，最常见的方法是夯土：先用木板做成一个框子，再把土倒进去，然后用工具一层一层地打结实。这样修出来的土墙非常结实，有的已经站了两千多年。在西边的沙漠里，土很少，人们就把沙子、小石头和芦苇一层一层地放在一起。

segs.en: By the Ming dynasty, wall-building techniques had made great progress.
In the mountains, builders used large stones for the lower part of the wall and bricks above.
The bricks were fired specially nearby, and some of them still bear the date and place they were made.
It is said that in some places rice soup made from glutinous rice was added to the lime, so that the bricks stuck together more firmly.
Scientists who studied this “sticky rice mortar” found that it really is very strong.

zh: 到了明朝，修长城的技术有了很大的进步。在山上，人们用大石头修墙的下面，上面再用砖。这些砖是在附近专门烧的，有的砖上还写着做砖的时间和地方。据说，有的地方在石灰里加了糯米汤，这样砖和砖之间就粘得更牢。科学家研究以后发现，这种“糯米灰浆”真的非常结实。

segs.en: Building the wall was extremely hard work.
Much of the wall stands on mountains where paths were hard to walk, and heavy stones and countless bricks all had to be carried up by people and animals.
It is said that in some places people stood in long lines and passed the bricks up the mountain one by one; others had goats carry bricks on their backs up the slopes.
The builders were soldiers, but also farmers and convicts, and many of them never returned home.

zh: 修长城是一件非常辛苦的工作。很多长城修在山上，路很难走，很重的石头和成千上万块砖都要靠人和动物运上去。据说，有的地方的人排成长队，一块一块地把砖传上山；还有人让山羊背着砖往上爬。修长城的人有士兵，也有农民和犯人，很多人再也没有回到家乡。

segs.en: The Great Wall is also more than just a wall.
At intervals along the wall stand watchtowers, where soldiers could live and where weapons and grain could be stored.
On the hills near the wall there are also many beacon towers.
If the enemy was spotted, the soldiers on the beacon towers sent up smoke by day and lit fires by night, so that people far away would know the enemy was coming.
Legend has it that people in ancient times burned wolf dung, because its smoke was black and rose straight up; that is why “wolf smoke” later came to mean war.
In the Ming dynasty, the number of smokes or fires, together with the number of cannon shots, was used to show how many enemies there were.
In this way, passing from one beacon tower to the next, news could travel hundreds of kilometres very quickly.

zh: 长城也不只是一道墙。墙上每隔一段就有一座敌楼，士兵可以住在里面，也可以在里面放武器和粮食。在长城附近的山上，还有很多烽火台。如果发现敌人，士兵就在烽火台上白天放烟，晚上点火，让远处的人知道敌人来了。传说古人会烧狼粪，因为它的烟又黑又直，所以“狼烟”后来成了战争的意思。明朝的时候，人们还用烟和火的数量，再加上放炮的次数，来表示敌人有多少。就这样，一个烽火台接一个烽火台，消息很快就能传到几百公里以外。

segs.en: Along the wall there are also many “passes”, places with gates where people and carts could go in and out.
The most famous are Shanhaiguan in the east and Jiayuguan in the west.

Shanhaiguan, close to the sea, is called “the First Pass Under Heaven”; Jiayuguan stands in the Gobi, and the deep silence all around it often makes visitors think of life on the frontier in ancient times.

zh: 长城上还有很多“关”，也就是有城门的地方，人和马车可以从这里进出。最有名的是东边的山海关和西边的嘉峪关。山海关靠近大海，被叫做“天下第一关”；嘉峪关在戈壁上，四周非常安静，常常让人想起古时候的边塞生活。

segs.en: Can You See the Great Wall from Space?

zh: 从太空能看到长城吗？

segs.en: Many people have heard the claim that the Great Wall is the only man-made structure that can be seen with the naked eye from space; some even say it can be seen from the moon.
The claim has appeared in many books and textbooks, but it is not true.

zh: 很多人都听过这样一种说法：长城是人们在太空中唯一能用眼睛看到的人造建筑，有人甚至说在月亮上也能看到。这种说法在很多书和课本里都出现过，可是它并不对。

segs.en: Although the wall is very long, it is not wide: in most places it is only a few metres across.
What is more, its colour is much the same as the hills and earth around it, so it is hard to pick out.
Looking down from space, several hundred kilometres up, it is almost impossible to see it with the naked eye; from the moon it is even less possible.
Someone once put it this way: looking for the Great Wall from the moon is like trying to see a single hair from five kilometres away.
In 2003, China's first astronaut, Yang Liwei, flew into space aboard Shenzhou 5.
When he came back, reporters asked him whether he had seen the Great Wall, and he answered that he had not.
However, using cameras with telephoto lenses and under very good conditions, astronauts have taken photographs of the wall.
So the greatness of the wall does not lie in whether it can be seen from space, but in its history and in the people who built it.

zh: 长城虽然很长，但是并不宽，大部分地方只有几米宽。而且，长城的颜色和周围的山、土差不多，很难分出来。从几百公里高的太空往下看，用眼睛几乎不可能看到它；从月亮上看就更不可能了。有人打了一个比方：从月亮上看长城，就像在五公里以外看一根头发。2003年，中国第一位航天员杨利伟坐“神舟五号”飞上了太空。回来以后，记者问他有没有看到长城，他回答说没有看到。不过，用相机和长焦镜头，在条件很好的时候，航天员拍到过长城的照片。所以，长城的伟大不在于能不能从太空看到，而在于它的历史和修建它的人。

segs.en: The Story of Meng Jiangnü
tok: Meng Jiangnü, heroine of a folk tale

zh: 孟姜女的故事

segs.en: The most famous folk tale about the wall is “Meng Jiangnü Weeps at the Great Wall”.
tok: “Meng Jiangnü Weeps at the Great Wall”

segs.en: Legend says that in the Qin dynasty there lived a young woman called Meng Jiangnü.
tok: Meng Jiangnü, heroine of a folk tale

segs.en: She had only just married her husband, Fan Xiliang, when he was seized by soldiers and sent north to work on the Great Wall.
Meng Jiangnü waited at home for a long time, but never heard any news of him.
tok: Meng Jiangnü, heroine of a folk tale

segs.en: As winter drew near, she worried that her husband would be cold, so she sewed winter clothes for him with her own hands and walked thousands of li alone to find him.

zh: 关于长城，最有名的民间故事是“孟姜女哭长城”。传说在秦朝的时候，有一个姑娘叫孟姜女。她刚刚和丈夫范喜良结婚，丈夫就被官兵抓走，送到北方去修长城了。孟姜女在家里等了很久，一直没有丈夫的消息。冬天快到了，她担心丈夫会冷，就亲手做了冬天的衣服，一个人走了几千里路去找他。

segs.en: But when at last she reached the foot of the wall, she was told that her husband had worked himself to death and been buried inside the wall.
Heartbroken, Meng Jiangnü sat down at the foot of the wall and began to weep.
tok: Meng Jiangnü, heroine of a folk tale

segs.en: She wept for three days and three nights until suddenly, with a great roar, a long stretch of the wall came crashing down, revealing her husband's bones.
This story is of course not real history, but it gives voice to the suffering of ordinary people.
Today there is still a Meng Jiangnü Temple near Shanhaiguan, and many tourists go there to have a look.

zh: 可是，等她终于走到长城下面的时候，别人告诉她，她的丈夫已经累死了，而且被埋在了长城里。孟姜女非常伤心，坐在长城下面大哭起来。她哭了三天三夜，突然“轰”的一声，一大段长城倒了下来，露出了丈夫的尸骨。这个故事当然不是真的历史，但是它说出了普通人的痛苦。今天，在山海关附近还有一座孟姜女庙，很多游客会去那里看一看。

segs.en: The Great Wall Today

zh: 今天的长城

segs.en: Chinese people like to say, “You are no true hero until you have reached the Great Wall.”
tok: “no true hero until you reach the Great Wall”

segs.en: It means that if you have never been to the Great Wall, you cannot count as a real hero.
So many people who come to Beijing make sure to go and climb the wall.
The most famous section is Badaling, sixty or seventy kilometres from the centre of Beijing; it is easy to get to, and you can even go there by high-speed train.
The wall at Badaling has been well restored and is fairly easy to walk on, but there are also enormous numbers of tourists; on public holidays it can be so crowded you can hardly move.
Nowadays you need to book online in advance to visit Badaling, and the number of visitors each day is limited.
If you would like fewer crowds, you can go to Mutianyu, where the scenery is beautiful too.

zh: 中国人常说：“不到长城非好汉”。意思是，没有去过长城，就不算真正的英雄。所以，很多来北京的人一定要去爬长城。最有名的是八达岭长城，它离北京市中心大约六七十公里，交通很方便，还可以坐高铁去。八达岭的长城修复得很好，路比较好走，但是游客也特别多，节假日的时候人多得几乎走不动。现在去八达岭需要提前在网上预约，每天的游客人数也有限制。如果想人少一点，可以去慕田峪，那里的风景也很美。

segs.en: Some sections of the wall have never been restored; people call them the “wild wall”.
The wild wall still looks the way it did centuries ago: grass and small trees grow all over it, and in places it has already collapsed.
Many people who like adventure find the wild wall more interesting, and more beautiful too.
But climbing the wild wall is very dangerous, people get hurt every year, and many wild sections are closed to visitors.

zh: 还有一些长城从来没有修复过，人们叫它们“野长城”。野长城保留着几百年前的样子，墙上长满了草和小树，有的地方已经倒了。很多喜欢冒险的人觉得野长城更有意思，也更漂亮。不过，爬野长城非常危险，每年都有人受伤，而且很多野长城是不允许游客进去的。

segs.en: Battered by wind and rain, and damaged by people as well, many sections of the wall are slowly disappearing.
In the past, some farmers took bricks from the wall home to build their houses; today, some tourists write on the wall or carve their names into it.
In 1987, the Great Wall became a World Cultural Heritage site.
China has also drawn up regulations to protect the wall, and when it is repaired, people try to use the original materials and methods, so that “the old is repaired to look old”.
tok: “repair the old so it stays old”

zh: 因为风吹雨打，再加上人的破坏，很多长城正在慢慢消失。过去，有的农民把长城上的砖拿回家盖房子；现在，也有游客在墙上写字、刻名字。1987年，长城成为了世界文化遗产。中国也制定了保护长城的法规，修复长城的时候，人们尽量用原来的材料和方法，做到“修旧如旧”。

segs.en: In Closing

zh: 结语

segs.en: The Great Wall was not built by one person or one dynasty, but little by little by many generations over more than two thousand years.
It may not be visible from space, but its stories, its history and the countless ordinary people who built it are all worth remembering.
Next time you stand on the Great Wall, touch the old bricks for a moment, and think of the people who carried them up the mountain hundreds of years ago.

zh: 长城不是一个人、一个朝代修的，而是很多代人用两千多年的时间一点一点修起来的。它也许不能从太空中看到，但是它的故事、它的历史，还有修建它的无数普通人，都值得我们记住。下次你站在长城上的时候，可以摸一摸那些旧砖，想一想几百年前把它们搬上山的人。
